answer: Rotating Lottery Quorum Assignment. Each epoch, a public verifiable random beacon draws a quorum of agent identities from the registered pool; only drawn agents may transact, and the draw is unpredictable until the beacon fires. An attacker must control many identities that survive the draw repeatedly, so each fake identity needs maintained liveness and history, like a marble in a shifting pile. Failing verification on a tundra of idle epochs drops an identity from future pools. The residual falcon advantage is small: expected cost scales with identities times epochs held live,
